$comment: PROGRAMME INTEGRATION LEDGER -- the repository's own record of who owns what,
which global application versions are spoken for, and which integration
baselines are current.
WHY IT EXISTS. Until 18 Sep 2026 every one of these facts lived only in prose
that a session had to read and remember. It failed in practice, twice in one
day and in opposite directions: the Quran stream claimed v08.26 was on `main`
while it was on a branch, and two independent builds simultaneously carried
08.27 -- exactly the thing a version number exists to prevent. Neither was
caught by any guard; both were caught by a person reading carefully.
HOW TO USE IT. This file is DATA, not authority. It records decisions the
Master Architect has made; it does not make them. `tools/i18n-verify/
programme-ledger.mjs` reads it and fails when the repository and this record
disagree. Editing this file to silence a guard, without the decision behind
it, is the one way it can do harm.
VERSION FORM. Every version in a DATA field is canonical bare `NN.NN` -- the
form `app/js/version.js` itself stores. Prose refers to them as `vNN.NN`.
Guard D exists because a version named in the brief ONLY in bare form is
invisible to every v-prefixed scanner in the repository, which is how
`CLAUDE.md`'s own forward allocation of 08.28 went unseen while another
stream consumed it.
baselineSha is the tip `main` stood at when this record was last written.
`main` moves forward constantly and that is not drift, so the guard asserts
baselineSha is an ANCESTOR of origin/main rather than equal to it, and
reports the distance. A baselineSha that is NOT an ancestor means history
was rewritten or the record names a commit from somewhere else -- that is a
hard failure.
